NAME: ConvLSTM-based fracture prediction model
TYPE: method

DIRECT_CLAIMS: The ConvLSTM model accurately predicts fracture patterns, crack‑length trends, and both mode‑I (tensile) and mode‑II (shear) loading responses across crystal orientations, closely matching atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, with only a minor discrepancy for the x100 orientation under mode‑II shear.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: The model predicts fracture toughness values that are comparable to those obtained from atomistic molecular dynamics simulations.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: A model trained exclusively on single‑crystal data generalizes to bicrystal and gradient‑orientation crystals, reproducing MD fracture patterns for small orientation differences, capturing overall crack paths for large orientation differences, and handling arbitrary geometry gradients.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: The ConvLSTM approach reduces computational cost dramatically compared with full molecular dynamics simulations, enabling rapid fracture predictions.
ARTICLE: Using Deep Learning to Predict Fracture Patterns in Crystalline Solids

NAME: GNoME
TYPE: method

DIRECT_CLAIMS: GNoME discovered 2.2 million crystal structures stable with respect to the Materials Project, with 381,000 newly on the convex hull, representing an order-of-magnitude expansion from all previous discoveries.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: 736 GNoME-discovered structures match experimentally validated ICSD structures, with 184 representing novel discoveries since the project began.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: GNoME achieves hit rates above 80% for structural predictions and 33% for composition-only predictions, compared to 1% in previous work, with active learning improving from less than 6% and 3% respectively over six rounds.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Final GNoME models predict energies with a mean absolute error of 11 meV per atom on relaxed structures, improved from 21 meV per atom in the initial model trained on Materials Project data.
ARTICLE: Matbench Discovery: A framework to evaluate machine learning crystal stability predictions

NAME: ML‑IAP
TYPE: method

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Using the frozen‑framework approximation, where only a single Li ion moves while the host lattice remains fixed, reduces the generalization error of the ML‑IAP compared with fully relaxed MD or NEB simulations.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: The proposed descriptor‑based screening approach is not tied to a specific ML‑IAP; it can be employed with any universal interatomic potential model.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Finite‑size tests using a larger supercell and an ML‑IAP (SevenNet) show that diffusion coefficients converge within statistical uncertainties, confirming that the AIMD results are not significantly affected by supercell size.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Using an ML‑trained interatomic potential (ML‑IAP) enables validation of many more candidate structures than conventional AIMD, as demonstrated by MD simulations on 30 random and 100 top‑Ξ structures.
ARTICLE: Predicting ionic conductivity in solids from the machine-learned potential energy landscape
